assumptions: the 3 shortest laws (from infinite systems) of every affine class that contains an infinite system - non-constant Q-gcd, classify() of EXP-C13-01 - and is not all N (3var<=4 and 2var<=5 families of EXP-C13-01); revised after the Skeptic's review, which found that the first filter (spectrum up to 120 reaching 60) also let in 52 laws from finite classes Div(L), L >= 61
N = 2..8; SAT with all affine tables blocked; conflict budget 300,000; UNKNOWN recorded
a first run (4 laws per class, N <= 9, budget 2,000,000) was stopped after 17 CPU-minutes
meta.falsification: A non-affine anchored model of any selected law.
meta.hypothesis: H-C13-2 (bold): for every law with at most 4 leaves per side (3 variables) or 5 leaves per side (2 variables) whose affine spectrum is infinite and not all N, every anchored model is affine.
meta.methodology: For each selected law and N, add one blocking clause per affine table x + a*y + 1 to the anchored SAT encoding; SAT means a non-affine model exists (the table is recorded for N <= 5), UNSAT means every model is affine.
meta.question: For laws whose affine spectrum is infinite but not all N (golden, x^2+x+1, -1 square, 2 square, odd, plastic, tribonacci, ...), does every anchored model of size N <= 8 come from an affine table x*y = x + a*y + 1? If so, the true spectrum agrees with the arithmetic set for N <= 8.
meta.title: Affine rigidity of laws with infinite non-trivial affine spectra

summary: 147 laws from infinite non-trivial affine classes tested for N = 2..8
